image_description: A studio product shot displaying a collection of black loudspeakers arranged against a neutral grey gradient background. The set includes multiple rectangular bookshelf speakers with circular drivers, a larger center-channel speaker with an angled front baffle, and smaller satellite speakers. The speakers feature glossy black enclosures and silver/grey metallic-looking driver cones.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All visible units exhibit standard rectangular prism geometries typical of speaker cabinets.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: One or more circular speaker cones on front face of varying sizes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Each speaker unit clearly displays at least one circular driver; the center channel has two distinct sizes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vertical arrangement of a larger lower driver and smaller upper driver is consistent across the main units.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cone surface made of paper, polypropylene, or composite with rubber surround.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The driver cones appear to have a metallic, brushed aluminum texture rather than the matte finish of paper or polypropylene. While metal cones exist, this deviates from the specific 'paper/poly' description in the checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Grille cloth or perforated metal may cover the drivers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No grilles are present; the drivers are fully exposed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Terminal connections visible on rear panel.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image angle shows only the front and side profiles; rear panels are completely occluded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wood, MDF, or plastic enclosure with black, white, or wood-grain finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Enclosures appear to be painted MDF or plastic with a high-gloss black finish, fitting the description.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The cones have an unnaturally uniform, smooth metallic sheen that lacks the microscopic texture variations (dust cap seams, cone ridges) usually visible in macro photography of real speakers. They look slightly 'airbrushed'.

The speaker stacked on the top right appears to lack a clear contact shadow where it meets the speaker below it, creating a slight 'floating' effect inconsistent with the lighting of the other objects.
The bottom edge of the center channel speaker blends slightly into the surface without a crisp hard edge, suggesting minor geometric softness.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of audio equipment and rule out misclassification as generic boxes or electronics.
To verify the spatial relationship between the stacked speakers and detect any floating artifacts or depth map inconsistencies.
To check for edge bleeding between the black gloss cabinets and the grey background, ensuring clean silhouettes.
To analyze the material properties of the speaker cones for signs of AI-generated smoothing or lack of physical detail.

focus_areas: Texture realism of speaker driver materials
Edge sharpness of glossy black surfaces
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'metallic' appearance of the speaker cones. Real speakers often have textured paper or woven Kevlar; these look like smooth gradients. Also, verify if the stacking of the top-right speaker is physically plausible given the lighting direction.
